newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pasifik Satelit announces Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Pasifik Satelit announces Q1 loss.

text.p: Indonesia's P.T. Pasifik Satelit Nusantara (PSN) reported a net loss of $1.14 million for the first three months of 1997 compared to an unaudited loss of $676,027 in the same period last year.

The company said in a statement released on Monday that it had audited total revenues of $4.28 million in the first quarter of 1997 representing a 10-fold increase over its unaudited revenues of $406,452 for the same period last year.
Gross profit increased from an unaudited $79,754 in 1996 to $1.75 million in the period under review, it said.

"The increase in the net loss in 1997 is largely attributable to costs for depreciation and operation of the Palapa C satellites, neither of which were in operation prior to June 1996," the statement said.
Revenues from the leasing of satellite transponders on Palapa C1 continued to be the mainstay of PSN's income in the first quarter endeed March 31, 1997, it said.

PSN owns six transponders on each of the Palapa C1 and Palapa C2 satellites, both of which were launched in the first half of 1996. Five of the six transponders on the Palapa C1 are currently leased to major Asian broadcasters including Star TV, NBC Asia, TVBI and RCTI.
